claims.text: High-entropy alloys comprise five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a simple solid-solution phase relative to intermetallic formation or phase segregation.
Differences in the atomic sizes of constituent elements cause lattice distortion in HEAs.
Structural and chemical stability over 473–1923 K is governed by the balance between configurational entropy and enthalpic factors such as atomic-size mismatch and specific interatomic interactions.
High mixing entropy promotes chemically disordered or random mixing in HEA solid solutions.
Short-range chemical ordering is an emergent mediator of HEA nanoparticle stability.
If lattice distortion and short-range ordering remain below a critical level, the homogeneous solid solution has lower free energy than phase-separated or intermetallic states.
The entropy-stabilized solid solution remains favored even under rapid thermal cycling.
Large atomic-radius differences or unfavorable bonding interactions can dominate the entropy contribution and cause phase segregation or chemical reconstruction.
Excessive lattice strain or pronounced short-range order raises local free energy enough to trigger phase segregation or surface reconstruction during temperature fluctuations.
Varying HEA composition can tune atomic-size mismatch and mixing enthalpy.
HEA nanoparticles with limited lattice strain and favorable mixing enthalpy will retain a single-phase solid solution and consistent surface properties throughout operation from 473 K to 1923 K.
Retention of structure and surface chemistry will yield stable catalytic activity or thermoelectric performance.
Compositions with excessive atomic-size mismatch will undergo phase decomposition or chemical reordering during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Near-ideal atomic-size compatibility and balanced interactions produce less segregation and more stable performance than deliberately mismatched compositions.
The proposed stabilization holds only while temperature-induced atomic mobility does not overcome kinetic retention of the homogeneous state.
Extremely unfavorable mixing enthalpy or extreme size mismatch is especially likely to cause deviation from the proposed behavior near 1923 K.
